concerns.text: FR-001 assumes the NASA Ames and University of Wisconsin battery datasets are publicly downloadable, but the project’s research documentation indicates these datasets are not available and a synthetic placeholder will be used. Without real multi‑channel time‑series data the requirement cannot be exercised, making the functional requirement untestable.

SC-004 states the model *aims* for an R² ≥ 0.80 on an unseen‑protocol subset. The word “aims” makes the success criterion non‑deterministic; a test must be able to declare pass/fail. Replace “aims” with a mandatory threshold (e.g., “must achieve”) or add a clear decision rule.

SC-005 requires measuring “percentage of cells successfully processed” but does not define the reference population (original dataset size after filtering, raw download size, etc.). Without a concrete denominator the metric cannot be reproducibly calculated.

SC-009 demands a held‑out test subset with at least 10 cells of unseen cycling protocols. The specification provides no guarantee that the public datasets contain that many distinct protocol types, so the input condition may be unreachable.

SC-003 and SC-008 both require a Spearman ρ ≥ 0.7 between permutation importance and SHAP rankings, resulting in duplicate success criteria. Consolidate to a single criterion to avoid unnecessary redundancy.
